summary.headline: NALCO Q1 FY27 total income rose about 39% YoY to INR 5,400 crore and PBT about 88%, with the 5th Stream refinery delayed to a late-2026 start.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the best-ever first quarter on revenue and profitability, with record bauxite, hydrate and wind power output. Total income rose from INR 3,930 crore to INR 5,400 crore, PBT grew about 88% and EBITDA about 78%. Raw material inflation of about INR 15,000-16,000 per tonne of metal (caustic soda, CP coke, HFO) was largely offset by spot alumina prices of about $370/t versus a Q1 realisation of about $323/t. The 5th Stream refinery (1 million tonne) has slipped by roughly 2-3 months, with mechanical completion now targeted for September-end 2026.

segments.name: Alumina
segments.commentary: Q1 realisation about $323/t; spot tenders in July-August about $370-380/t, with management guiding Q2 average near $370/t. Alumina sales target FY27 is 1.6 million tonnes versus about 1.4 million tonnes last year.

segments.name: Aluminium (metal)
segments.commentary: Production was at about 4.72 lakh tonnes last year, with FY27 guided to about 4.76-4.77 lakh tonnes and a possible 4.75 lakh tonne run-rate. Domestic prices are LME plus premium from export tenders, with the premium reset every 3-4 months. LME was about $3,200/t at the call.

segments.name: Captive coal
segments.commentary: Q1 output was 8.80 lakh tonnes after about 5 days of technical outage at the start of the quarter. FY27 target is 4.8 million tonnes, against about 4 million tonnes last year, with the EC expected in about 2-3 months. Captive landed cost is about INR 1,600/t versus e-auction coal at INR 3,500-3,600/t.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Record Q1 wind power generation was reported. A 1,080 MW power plant is planned as a 50:50 JV with NLC, with a 30:70 debt-equity structure.

guidance_outlook: 5th Stream refinery (1 Mt) mechanical completion by September-end 2026, then integrated trials. Stabilisation takes 3-4 months to reach 60-70%; about 2 lakh tonnes of alumina is still targeted in FY27.
Alumina capacity goes from 2.1 Mt to a rated 3.1 Mt from FY28, with 3.2-3.3 Mt targeted. Bauxite output is about 2.2-2.3 Mt today.
Captive coal target 4.8 Mt in FY27. Pottangi mine production expected from October 2026 after road work.
Metal cost of about INR 1,70,000-1,72,000/t in Q2. Alumina cost guided at INR 21,000-22,000/t. Alumina spot realisation expected at about $370/t, roughly $50 above the Q1 average.

Smelter expansion of 0.5 Mt with a 1,000+ MW power plant is targeted for Board approval around October-November 2026 and completion by December 2030. Total capex is about INR 24,000-25,000 crore to FY31.
FY27 capex target INR 1,500-1,800 crore, rising to about INR 2,500 crore in FY28 and then INR 4,000-7,000 crore per year thereafter.
Employee count is 4,848 as of Q1 end, with a 170-200 reduction each year over the next 3-4 years. A pay revision from 1 January 2027 may add about 15% to employee cost in Q4.
capex_capacity: 5th Stream refinery: 1 Mt alumina, about INR 5,600 crore cost, internally funded. Commissioning delayed by about 2-3 months from the June target.
Smelter expansion: 0.5 Mt aluminium, EGA technology licence to be signed about August 2026. DPR in 3-4 months, with package ordering in about 8-9 months.

Power: 1,080 MW JV with NLC (50:50), total cost about INR 12,000 crore, NALCO share about INR 6,000 crore with equity about INR 3,500 crore total and bank debt guaranteed by NALCO. Coal is sourced from NLC mines in Talcher.
Captive coal expansion: 4.8 Mt, EC expected in 2-3 months. Pottangi bauxite mine MDO appointed, but production is held up by local resistance over an 8 km access road.
Panchpatmali bauxite reserve about 110 Mt plus new mines of about 100-120 Mt, giving a 15-20 year balance life at about 8 Mtpa.
demand_pricing: Alumina spot prices rose on Rusal and Chinese refinery red-mud curtailments and higher New Guinea bauxite costs. About 60-70% of alumina goes to the Middle East.
Alumina realisation is now about 10-11% of LME, down from 14-15%. Management sees 11-12% as the long-run level.
Domestic aluminium premium rose to about $110/t from about $60/t, attributed to Middle East war supply disruption. Management expects it to hold or fall as the war eases.
Input costs: caustic soda about INR 45,000/t in Q1 rising to about INR 49,000/t in Q2, CP coke INR 66,000-70,000/t (vs INR 44,000 last year), HFO INR 75,000/t (vs INR 46,000 last year).
Industry metal deficit of about 0.88 Mt is cited, with LME forecast at $3,000-3,200/t for the rest of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the 5th Stream refinery commissioning delayed by about 6 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Mechanical completion slipped by 2-3 months. Over 50 packages are in progress and mechanical completion is targeted for September-end, followed by water runs and then production. Output of about 2 lakh tonnes of alumina is still targeted in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall, and will it stay low through FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Average CTC fell from about INR 36 lakh to INR 33 lakh due to superannuation of high-paid staff and entry-level hiring. Last year's provisions for leave and gratuity and lower PRP accruals also contributed, and the trend should continue for the next three quarters. Q4 will rise because of the pay revision.

qa_highlights.question: Will raw material cost inflation erode margins as aluminium prices soften?
qa_highlights.answer: Metal cost rose about INR 15,000-16,000/t from raw materials. Management said higher alumina prices (about $370/t against a $320 expectation) should offset this, and Q2 metal cost is guided at INR 1,70,000-1,72,000/t.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any LME-linked alumina term contract for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: The term contracts earlier this year priced at about 10% of LME and were cancelled. Management will only tender when it gets better percentages, around 12-14% of LME.

qa_highlights.question: Coal stocks and monsoon risk for the refineries?
qa_highlights.answer: Captive coal covers about 60-70% of smelter power needs at Angul. Refinery coal stock is only 2-3 days against a 10-15 day norm because of rake priority to power plants. Management expects improvement after summer.

qa_highlights.question: How will the smelter and power capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Total capex to FY31 is about INR 24,000 crore, with the JV's 30:70 debt-equity split. NALCO's cash reserves of about INR 10,500 crore and internal accruals of about INR 3,500 crore a year are expected to fund the smelter without new borrowing.

risks_watch: 5th Stream refinery mechanical completion by September-end and ramp-up to 60-70% over 3-4 months. Any further slip affects the 2 lakh tonne FY27 target.
Refinery coal stock at 2-3 days against a 10-15 day norm during monsoon, dependent on rake allocation.
Pottangi mine start-up depends on the 8 km access road amid local resistance. Target is October 2026.
Domestic premium of about $110/t may fall as Middle East supply normalises. Spot alumina at about $370/t may also soften.
Captive coal EC approval expected in 2-3 months to reach 4.8 Mt.
Pay revision from January 2027 adds to Q4 employee cost. The 0.5 Mt smelter Board approval is expected in October-November 2026.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, realisations and cash generation, with Q1 presented as a best-ever quarter. Cautious on timelines, with the 5th Stream delay and the Pottangi access road both acknowledged as uncertain. Some answers were evasive or deferred to follow-up, notably the coal linkage/e-auction split and the premium breakup.
key_quotes: Our target is by September end, we have to complete mechanical completion of all these packages, do the integrated trial first.
Premium has increased. Our earlier premium was around $60. Now it has gone up to around -- we did the tender last around $110.
We have a balance of INR 10,500 crores now every year, seeing our profitability and the PAT, we are adding INR3,500-plus crores, because we are expecting earning the PAT of INR 6,000-plus crores.
So, we need not go to the market for borrowing for our smelter expansion, see, our cash reserve and our future earning potential.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 alumina sales to 1.6 Mt (vs ~1.4 Mt) and captive coal to 4.8 Mt (vs ~4 Mt), backed by the 5th Stream refinery (~2 lakh t alumina in FY27, but delayed 2-3 months to Sep-end 2026 mechanical completion) and Q2 alumina realisation near $370/t, though no explicit revenue growth figure was given.
